subject: Dedicated pool sizing for Visium Health - APAC primary, EU PHI fallback
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@visiumhealth.com>, Claire Park <cpark@visiumhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 09:12 PDT
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing for Visium Health - APAC primary, EU PHI fallback

Hi Simon / Claire —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I attached a quick snapshot of your observed traffic and the mutual action plan (visium_usage_snapshot.csv, visium_mop_v1.pdf). Key asks from your side:
- APAC-first deployment (Singapore) for low-latency clinical workflows
- EU region (Ireland) must be available as PHI-compliant fallback for certain EU customers
- Target go-live: week of 2026-11-08
- Expected Q1 steady-state: ~3k daily active requests + periodic batch exports (approx 45k tokens/day)

Next step from our side is to propose a dedicated pool sizing recommendation that meets your latency SLOs (~200–300ms 95th for generate flows) while keeping commit size predictable. Marcus / Soojin / Olga — can you take a look at the attached usage snapshot and propose a minimal dedicated configuration (steady + burst capacity) that we can turn into a PO?

Simon / Claire — feel free to reply with any additional constraints (data residency, encryption, certs) we should account for.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: visium_usage_snapshot.csv (csv), visium_mop_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@visiumhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 10:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Visium Health - APAC primary, EU PHI fallback

Jordan / team —

Quick, high-level sizing based on the snapshot and target SLOs:
- Baseline (steady): 8 x A100-equivalent (80GB) GPUs in APAC to cover sustained daytime load (3k DAU, typical concurrency peaks ~120 concurrent generation streams).
- Burst: additional 8 x A100-equivalent as burst pool (auto-burst up to 16 total) for peak batch windows / retraining prep. Burst capacity can be on shorter reservation (monthly) or metered.
- EU fallback: 6 x A40/40GB-equivalent nodes (or 3 x 80GB with shared KV cache) to keep PHI traffic resident. This is primarily for failover and for EU-only customers — expect low steady RPS but stringent residency/crypto requirements.

Operational notes:
- Recommend enabling prefix KV caching for common clinical prompts (saves ~30–45% tokens at inference).
- Use int8 quantization profile for non-PHI flows to reduce cost on burst jobs; keep full precision for PHI paths unless validated.
- Canary: provision 2x smaller nodes in US region for cross-region failover tests.

Cost levers to discuss with Visium: commit vs burst mix (reserving 12 GPUs across APAC/EU reduces per-GPU cost vs fully metered burst).

I'll draft a concrete config and estimated monthly commit by EOB today.

—Marcus
Head of Sales — Capacity & Enterprise

[Quoted attachments referenced by Jordan]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@visiumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-15 08:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Visium Health - APAC primary, EU PHI fallback

Marcus / team —

Supply constraints and short notes from sourcing for APAC (Singapore) and EU (Ireland):
- APAC: A100-80GB immediate availability limited; we can mix 80GB + 40GB nodes behind our runtime. For the same memory footprint, two 40GB nodes can host similar KV cache if we shard smartly but adds operational complexity.
- EU: A40/40GB is available on reservation; cross-region replication adds ~15% overhead to storage costs.

Proposed alternative sizing (supply-aware):
- APAC steady: 6 x A100-80GB + 4 x A40-40GB (as hot-standby burst); effective capacity similar to 10–11 80GB equivalents if we allow dynamic placement.
- EU fallback: 4 x 40GB reserved, with 1 dedicated 80GB for large PV/exports during scheduled windows.

Lead time: 3–5 business days to lock reservations in APAC once PO hits procurement. If Visium needs guaranteed 80GB-only nodes, add a 2–3 week lead time.

Attached a short supply snapshot.

—Soojin
Head of Sourcing (Capacity) | Redwood Inference

Attachments: apac_supply_snapshot.pdf (pdf)
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@visiumhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Park <cpark@visiumhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15 11:00 PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Visium Health - APAC primary, EU PHI fallback

Jordan / team —

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- EU residency is non-negotiable for all patient-identifiable workflows; EU must be the default for EU-sourced data. APAC (SG) is preferred for low-latency clinical UI.
- Our go-live is target week of 2026-11-08; we need a technical proof-of-concept (canary) in the EU by 2026-10-28 for internal compliance review.
- Can you confirm encrypted-at-rest with our KMS (we'll share the key material through the secure channel) and SOC2 acceptable controls list?
- On capacity: the numbers are plausible. Prefer reserve agreement that lets us burst cross-region for emergencies but keeps EU traffic resident by default.

If you can send an updated PO-friendly config + DocuSign for the reserve terms, we can route to procurement this week.

—Simon
Director, Engineering — Visium Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-16 09:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Visium Health - APAC primary, EU PHI fallback

Simon / Claire —

Summary and next steps (agreed actions):
1) Capacity commits:
   - APAC (SG): 12 A100-equivalent capacity (6x 80GB + 6x 40GB acting as hot-burst) reserved to deliver steady + burst.
   - EU (IE): 6 x 40GB reserved, with 1x 80GB reserved for scheduled exports/canary tests. EU remains the default for PHI workflows.
   - US: 2 smaller nodes for cross-region canary only (no PHI).
2) Timeline:
   - EU canary by 2026-10-28 (Soojin to confirm node provisioning timeline once PO is in).
   - Full APAC steady pool to be reserved within 5 business days of signed PO; target live by 2026-11-08.
3) Security / compliance:
   - We will enable KMS-based encryption for EU resident data and share SOC2 checklist in the secure folder (Olga will handle).
4) Commercials:
   - Drafted commit configuration attached and DocuSign envelope (placeholder). HubSpot deal: HS-84921; Deal ID: DEAL-2026-0042.

Action items: Marcus to send PO-friendly config & monthly commit estimate (today). Olga to upload SOC2 checklist & KMS onboarding steps. Soojin to confirm exact provisioning SLAs for APAC/EU. Simon to route DocuSign to procurement when ready.

I'll follow up with the PO/DocuSign link once Marcus confirms numbers.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
